refutations.argument: Game-state simulation of the commonest Commander ending. Three players, free-for-all, no range of influence. Nobody has lost. Player C resolves Thassa's Oracle and its ability states that C wins the game. By 104.2b an effect may do that, and by 104.1 the game ends immediately. Under 104.3 the ways to lose are concession, state-based actions and an effect stating that THAT player loses; none applies to A or B, so neither of them has lost the game in the CR's sense. CR 104.3h shows that the CR makes a winning effect cause the opponents to lose only in the limited-range-of-influence option; outside it no rule does. So in this game the revised rule's condition 'the previous game was won by one player and more than one player lost it' is false, and its tie-break 'several players lost first at the same moment' has no one to speak of. The revised rule is therefore silent exactly where the fix claims to give an answer, and 103.1's 'the loser of the previous game' still has no referent in the commonest way a multiplayer game ends. The same holds when A lost earlier and B did not: only A 'lost', so the rule's 'more than one lost' trigger never fires and the stipulation does not pick A by its own words. The stipulation must say that players still in the game when another player wins by an effect count as having lost it, and at the same moment; as worded it leaves this game type uncovered.

source.excerpt: An effect may state that a player wins the game.

steps.conclusion: In a free-for-all game one player can win by an effect (Thassa's Oracle) while the other players are still in the game and have not conceded, been caught by a state-based action, or been named by an effect that they lose.

steps.conclusion: The CR has a winning effect make opponents lose only under the limited range of influence option; in an ordinary free-for-all game won by an effect the opponents are not stated to have lost, so 'more than one player lost it' and 'lost first at the same moment' in C3 are not met and the rule names no chooser.
